papers.title: TEFAR: a lightweight, configurable framework for semi-automatic artefact component classification in EEG and TMS-EEG
papers.summary: TEFAR is a lightweight, configurable FieldTrip-based framework for semi-automatic artefact component classification in EEG and TMS-EEG, using robust statistics and signature-based detectors for artefacts including TMS decay and recharge. In 30 ground-truth simulations, it achieved specificity of 1.000 and sensitivity of 0.96-0.97 for both profiles.

papers.title: Multidomain Electroencephalography Biomarker Fusion for Machine Learning-Based Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: Evaluated multidomain resting-state EEG biomarkers (RMS, power spectral density, entropy) plus demographic features for machine learning classification of Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls in 88 participants using a Random Forest classifier with explainable AI. The full model achieved 96% training and 92% test accuracy, and removing entropy features increased test accuracy to 94%.

papers.title: Intermittent Cranial Accelerometric Pulses - a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease
papers.summary: This preprint identifies a novel phenomenon of brief periodic 'Sleep Bursts' in cranial forces during human sleep, occurring less frequently in subjects with neurodegenerative disease. EEG delta power during bursts was significantly lower in NDD subjects, suggesting a potential glymphatic drainage marker.

papers.title: The Dry Truth: Hair-Wetting Improves Dry Electrode EEG Signal Quality
papers.summary: In 22 healthy participants, hair-wetting reduced mean dry electrode EEG impedance by 75.7%, cut bad channels from ~40% to 15%, and increased spectral-power and functional-connectivity similarity with gel recordings by 7.7% and 56–70%, respectively. The method improves dry EEG signal quality but does not fully match gel-based systems.

papers.title: EEGDM: Label-Efficient EEG Representation Learning with Generative Diffusion Model.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: EEGDM is a diffusion-based EEG representation learning framework that uses a Structured State-Space Model for Diffusion Pretraining and a Latent Fusion Module for downstream tasks. It achieved competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art methods on EEG event classification, seizure detection, and seizure classification benchmarks while requiring substantially fewer samples for pretraining and adaptation.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Assessment of Sleepiness from Fingertip Pulse Wave Analysis During Objective Daytime Testing.
papers.summary: A deep learning sleep staging model was tested on fingertip photoplethysmography during MSLT and MWT to classify sleepy versus non-sleepy subjects. It reached 80% accuracy in MSLT and 83% in MWT, but direct zero-shot application to MWT showed limited sleep precision, indicating feasibility mainly in MSLT.

papers.title: A Patient-Specific Framework for Separating Temporal Localization from Intracranial Waveform Reconstruction of Interictal Epileptiform Discharges from Scalp EEG
papers.summary: A patient-specific dual-branch convolutional-attention framework separated temporal localization from event-specific intracranial waveform reconstruction of interictal epileptiform discharges using simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG in six subjects. Scalp EEG supported temporal localization above chance in three of six subjects, but event-specific waveform reconstruction was not consistently better than a fixed patient-specific template.

papers.title: Individual Differences in Neural Decoding Are Stable but Instrument Dependent
papers.summary: The study compared individual differences in neural decoding across EEG, MEG, intracranial EEG, and fMRI using excluded runs and stimulus identities for testing. Stable decoding differences were reproducible within instruments but instrument-dependent, explained partly by source-to-sensor distance and local category selectivity.

papers.title: Degraded neural representations foreshadow failures of sustained attention
papers.summary: EEG decoding during a sustained attention task showed that neural representational fidelity for task-relevant items weakened in poor attentional states and foreshadowed behavioral lapses. Pre-item representational strength predicted target memory success, implicating degraded neural representations in attentional disengagement.

papers.title: Pre-treatment EEG microstates and response to antipsychotic drugs in first episode psychosis
papers.summary: In 56 minimally treated first-episode psychosis patients, baseline resting-state EEG microstate PC1 predicted 12-week antipsychotic treatment response (adjusted OR=0.63, AUC=72.3% with clinical information). Microstate architecture deviating from a healthy-control-derived norm was associated with lower odds of treatment response.

papers.title: Enhanced cortical tracking of unfamiliar languages in both monolinguals and bilinguals
papers.summary: Using EEG and temporal response function modeling in 24 English monolinguals and 24 English-Mandarin bilinguals, this study tested cortical tracking of speech envelopes in familiar (English), bilingual-familiar (Mandarin), and unfamiliar (Vietnamese) languages. Both groups showed enhanced cortical tracking for unfamiliar languages, and bilinguals showed stronger overall tracking than monolinguals across all languages.

papers.title: Current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for EEG in dogs, showing that protocols vary substantially in stimulus design, vigilance state, and electrode montage. It proposes a framework for standardized awake testing and improved spatial sampling to enhance diagnostic sensitivity and translational alignment.

papers.title: Analysis of the influence of gradual changes in matrix sentence similarity on neural envelope tracking
papers.summary: This study used simultaneous MEG, 76-channel EEG, and ear-EEG from 21 normal-hearing adults to quantify how acoustic sentence similarity affects neural tracking of speech, using the Oldenburger Sentence Test matrix and audiobook-based decoder training. Significant reconstruction accuracies occurred for both heard and unheard sentences, and accuracies for mismatched sentences gradually increased with acoustic similarity, demonstrating potential spurious tracking in matrix tests while supporting ear-EEG viability.

papers.title: Patterns of Alpha-band Power Reflect Prioritization of the Most Recently Encoded Location in a Working Memory Sequence.
papers.summary: Two EEG experiments with inverted encoding models tested whether alpha-band power tracks locations of sequentially presented items during working memory maintenance. Alpha-band patterns tracked the most recently presented item in both experiments, while Item 1 was tracked longer in the spatial than color task, indicating covert spatial attention prioritizes one item at a time in a sequence.

papers.title: Cortical Spectral Dynamics in Flow and Frustration
papers.summary: EEG data from ten adults performing go and stop-signal tasks with continuously adjusted difficulty were analyzed for spectral dynamics during flow versus frustration, alongside subjective flow ratings. In the flow block, stop-trial errors coincided with pre-stimulus reductions in right temporoparietal gamma power, frontal beta and gamma power, and frontotemporal gamma coherence, while frustration showed higher temporal beta power.

papers.title: Subregion-specific temporal lobe EEG signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: Evidence from high-density EEG.
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state 128-channel high-density EEG in 55 individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 35 cognitively normal controls to characterize temporal-subregional electrophysiological features. Individuals with aMCI showed increased gamma-band activity across bilateral temporal subregions, elevated delta power and theta/beta ratios mainly in right temporal subregions, enhanced fast-frequency coupling, and gamma measures from left temporal subregions achieved discriminatory performance comparable to whole-temporal measures.

papers.title: Longitudinal adaptations in neural and behavioral systems following hearing restoration using cochlear implants.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This longitudinal study followed 19 newly implanted adult cochlear implant users over 12 months, measuring speech recognition, spatial hearing, quality of life, and EEG neural tracking during a continuous-speech selective-attention task. Speech recognition and spatial-separation benefits improved, task-relevant neural tracking was stronger and earlier than task-irrelevant tracking, and stronger task-relevant tracking correlated with better speech recognition, spatial listening, and quality of life, with gains plateauing by about 6 months.

papers.title: Brain-Wave Music Enhances Inhibitory Control Performance by Modulating Oscillations in the Motor Cortex and Frontoparietal Network.
papers.summary: Seventy-two healthy participants underwent a music intervention with four types of musical stimuli, including brain-wave music synthesized from individual neural oscillations, with Go/Nogo tasks and EEG before and after. Brief exposure to personalized brain-wave music enhanced inhibitory control performance, modulated frontal and parietal theta oscillations beyond stimulation, and behavioral improvement correlated with alignment between music and intrinsic neural patterns.

papers.title: Continuous Versus Routine EEG in Critically Ill Patients Without Primary Neurologic Condition: Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a post hoc analysis of the multicenter randomized CERTA trial restricted to 76 critically ill adults without primary neurologic conditions, continuous EEG was not associated with 6-month mortality, functional outcome, seizure detection, or medication changes compared with two routine EEG recordings. No seizures or status epilepticus were detected in either group, suggesting repeated routine EEG may be a reasonable alternative in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Case Studies in Identifying and Understanding Seizure Liability in Drug Development.
papers.summary: This review uses nonclinical case studies from drug development to outline a flexible workflow for identifying and mitigating drug-induced seizure liability, including seizure detection procedures, neurological findings that indicate risk, event patterns warranting EEG studies, and principles for mitigating liability during clinical trials. It provides a logical nonclinical testing approach aimed at protecting patient safety.

papers.title: Aberrant Neural Outputs and Disrupted Neural Oscillations of the Cerebellar Nuclei in a Mouse Model of Fragile X Syndrome.
papers.summary: Using Fmr1-knockout mice, this study mapped deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) projections and recorded in vivo electrophysiology to examine cerebellar output in Fragile X syndrome. It found target-specific alterations in DCN forebrain projections, disrupted neuronal firing patterns, loss of specific neuronal subtypes, and aberrant local field potential oscillations with weakened theta, alpha, and beta power despite unchanged gamma power, without morphological changes.

papers.title: Electrophysiological brain reconfiguration during meditation-induced extended cessation of consciousness: an EEG microstate study
papers.summary: This EEG microstate study examined five highly trained meditators during meditation-induced extended cessation (EC) of consciousness and compared it with counting and memory tasks. EC was associated with reduced microstate B (self-related processing), increased microstate C (integrative activity), and preferential routing of sensory-related microstate A toward integrative rather than self-related processing, indicating a distinct neural signature of transiently suspended consciousness.

papers.title: Mu suppression reveals auditory-motor predictions after short musical training.
papers.summary: Twenty-five non-musicians learned a simple melody on a piano-like keyboard while EEG was recorded, then passively listened to trained and control melodies before and after training. Mu suppression emerged before each note only for the practiced melody after training, indicating that short motor training supports single-note-level auditory-motor predictions independent of prior musical experience.

papers.title: AAV-mediated TBR1 supplementation ameliorates behavioral and electrophysiological abnormalities in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice
papers.summary: This study tested AAV-mediated human TBR1 supplementation in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice via retroorbital injection at postnatal day 3, assessing protein levels, cell counts, behavior, and EEG. Treatment increased TBR1 protein and TBR1-, CTIP2-, and parvalbumin-positive cell counts, improved sociability and food-seeking behaviors, and attenuated elevated relative theta power and improved theta suppression and gamma enhancement during social interaction, although some anatomical and EEG abnormalities persisted.

papers.title: Toward selective vowel-tone integration in non-tonal L2 learners of Mandarin: Evidence from MMN additivity.
papers.summary: EEG mismatch negativity additivity was used to test consonant, vowel, and tone integration in 24 native Mandarin listeners and 15 non-tonal L2 learners of Mandarin during a passive oddball task. L1 listeners showed sub-additive MMN patterns across all dimension pairs, whereas L2 learners showed additivity for consonant-vowel and consonant-tone but a selective sub-additive trend for vowel-tone, interpreted as preliminary evidence for vowel-tone integration.

papers.title: Use of an AI agent to improve epilepsy diagnosis.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared an AI-driven History of Present Illness tool with resident-recorded histories in 40 consecutive epilepsy monitoring unit patients, using video-EEG as the diagnostic gold standard. Resident histories were adequate for diagnosis in 58% of cases and yielded 58% expert diagnostic accuracy, while the AI Epilepsy HPI tool achieved 90% diagnostic accuracy and improved expert accuracy to 80%.

papers.title: Predicting the immediate and subsequent effects of commercials on product valuation using EEG and deep learning
papers.summary: This neuromarketing study recorded EEG from 161 participants while they viewed commercials and measured willingness to pay (WTP) immediately and one week later. Deep learning models applied to raw EEG achieved substantially higher predictive accuracy than standard EEG measures, successfully predicting immediate and delayed WTP and ad liking, including for new participants and products, though accuracy declined with increasing generalization demands and narrower value differences.

papers.title: The Role of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Peripheral Nerves and Skeletal Muscle Function in Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.journal: Journal of the ASEAN Federation of Endocrine Societies
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 32 studies mapped evidence on SGLT2 inhibitors' effects on peripheral nerves and skeletal muscle in type 2 diabetes, finding potential improvements in nerve conduction velocity, epidermal nerve fiber density, and muscle substrate flexibility, but divergent or neutral functional outcomes and a predominance of animal models.

papers.title: Multimodal predictors of response to intravenous ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: toward personalized treatment in major depressive and bipolar disorders.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided review of 150 studies synthesized multimodal predictors of intravenous ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression, identifying baseline severity, inflammatory and neuroplastic biomarkers, metabolic factors, genetic variants, neurophysiological signatures, and early symptomatic improvement as key predictors, and proposed a preliminary framework for personalized treatment.

papers.title: Diffusion MRI abnormalities localise the epileptogenic zone in paediatric drug-resistant epilepsy
papers.summary: In children with drug-resistant epilepsy, diffusion MRI abnormalities predicted seizure freedom when resected (OR 1.31 per 10% overlap, AUC 0.723) and aligned with stereo-EEG seizure-onset zones and PET hypometabolism, supporting their role in presurgical evaluation.

papers.title: Nociception monitoring during cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: limitations and future directions.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: This review discusses physiological limitations affecting intraoperative nociception monitoring during cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, noting that current surrogate autonomic, vascular, pupillary, and EEG-derived signals become difficult to interpret during CPB and that cardiac-specific validation remains limited, and highlights priorities for future validation and context-aware analytics.

papers.title: Morphosyntactic processing of complex nonwords in sentence context: An ERP study.
papers.summary: This ERP study investigated how suffixes in nonwords are processed in syntactically congruent and incongruent sentence contexts. It found larger positive amplitudes for non-suffixes than suffixes across multiple time windows and a larger P600 for incongruent than congruent stimuli, suggesting rapid morphosyntactic integration based on suffix information.

papers.title: Sodium Valproate-Induced Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 63-year-old woman on long-term valproic acid who developed encephalopathy with marked sinus bradycardia despite normal serum ammonia and therapeutic valproate levels. Discontinuation of valproate led to complete resolution of both encephalopathy and bradycardia.

papers.title: A Multisystem Presentation of West Nile Neuroinvasive Disease: Lessons in Diagnostic Complexity.
papers.summary: A case report of a 61-year-old man presenting with fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, and confusion initially mimicking tick-borne illness and thyroid storm. West Nile neuroinvasive disease was confirmed by CSF IgM on hospital day eight after a complicated hospital course.

papers.title: Development of a prospective clinical workflow for proton beam therapy of ventricular tachycardia.
papers.journal: Strahlentherapie und Onkologie : Organ der Deutschen Rontgengesellschaft ... [et al]
papers.summary: This technical feasibility study developed a prospective preclinical workflow for proton beam therapy of refractory ventricular tachycardia, covering electroanatomical mapping (EAM)-to-CT target transfer, treatment planning using three STOPSTORM.eu benchmark cases, and synchrotron beam gating integration. Treatment plans achieved effective organ-at-risk sparing with PTV D95% of 23.3–23.9 Gy (RBE), CTV(EP) D95% of 30.9–31.6 Gy (RBE), no CTV(EP) hotspot above 33.5 Gy (RBE), and total cardiac gating chain latency below 30 ms, demonstrating technical feasibility while full clinical translation requires further validation.

papers.title: Breaking the link between demyelination and axon loss: SARM1 inhibition as a neuroprotective strategy for multiple sclerosis
papers.summary: This preclinical study tested SARM1 inhibition in optic nerve crush and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models using knockout mice, AAV-mediated CRISPR, and the small molecule 5-iodoisoquinoline. SARM1 inhibition preserved axons and visual function and reduced serum neurofilament light chain without affecting demyelination or gross inflammation, indicating it can uncouple axon loss from demyelination.

papers.title: Architected Load Paths Enable Stiffening and Motion Programming in Soft Pneumatic Actuators.
papers.summary: MARS, a monolithic architected reinforcement strategy for soft pneumatic actuators, embeds internal beam-column load paths that suppress ballooning, maintain intended morphology up to 200 kPa, increase lateral stiffness 5.8-fold, and generate 8.4-fold higher tip force than a baseline, with programmable variants enabling crawling, grasping, and wearable hand assistance.

papers.title: A Comparison of Safety and Outcome Using Three Different Sedation Strategies During Pulsed Field Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: In a nationwide cohort of 1269 patients undergoing first-time pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation, deep sedation managed by electrophysiology staff or anesthesia nurses was feasible with few sedation-related adverse events and no differences in 1-year atrial tachycardia recurrence compared to general anesthesia.

papers.title: Systems-Level in Silico Bioinformatic Profiling Identifies Key Hub Genes and Potential Therapeutic Targets in Atrial Fibrillation without Overt Comorbidity.
papers.journal: Research in heart yield and translational medicine
papers.summary: An in silico bioinformatics analysis identified 81 genes associated with atrial fibrillation without overt comorbidity, with protein-protein interaction network enrichment and DMNC ranking highlighting 10 hub genes, including GPD1L, SCN1B, SCN4B, and KCNE2, centered on cardiac action potential and contraction pathways.

papers.title: Podocarpane diterpenoids with various subtypes from Strophioblachia glandulosa Pax var. cordifolia combined with fluconazole activation of the Hog1 pathway demonstrating antifungal activity.
papers.summary: From Strophioblachia glandulosa var. cordifolia, eight diterpenoids including seven new compounds were isolated and characterized; compounds 7 and 8 showed significant synergistic antifungal activity with fluconazole against resistant Candida albicans, and compound 8 was found to act by activating the Hog1 pathway to suppress hyphal formation.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
